title: What studying twins can teach us about ourselves, with Nancy Segal, PhD

sentences.en: Twins have long captured the public imagination.
sentences.zh: 双胞胎长期以来一直吸引着公众的想象力。

sentences.en: Movie plots, ad campaigns, viral videos of twin toddlers babbling at each other in what seems like a secret language.
sentences.zh: 电影情节、广告活动、双胞胎幼儿似乎在使用某种秘密语言对彼此牙牙学语的病毒视频。

sentences.en: Something about twins grabs our attention every time.
sentences.zh: 关于双胞胎的某些特质总能每次都抓住我们的注意力。

sentences.en: But it's not only the general public that's fascinated with twins.
sentences.zh: 但不仅是普通大众对双胞胎着迷。

sentences.en: Twins have also garnered their share of attention from psychologists and other researchers
sentences.zh: 双胞胎也从心理学家和其他研究人员那里获得了相当多的关注，

sentences.en: because of what they can tell us about how our genes and environment interact to make us who we are.
sentences.zh: 因为他们能告诉我们基因与环境如何相互作用来造就今天的我们。

sentences.en: Where is twin research today?
sentences.zh: 如今的双胞胎研究进展如何？

sentences.en: As our understanding of human genetics has advanced in recent years, do twin studies remain vital?
sentences.zh: 随着近年来我们对人类遗传学理解的深入，双胞胎研究依然至关重要吗？

sentences.en: What about twins who are raised apart and meet later in life?
sentences.zh: 那些从小分开抚养、在晚年相遇的双胞胎呢？

sentences.en: What can we learn from those natural experiments?
sentences.zh: 我们能从这些自然实验中学到什么？

sentences.en: And why are so many people, scientists and laypeople alike, so fascinated with twins?
sentences.zh: 为什么那么多人，无论是科学家还是外行，都对双胞胎如此着迷？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: If you enjoy Speaking of Psychology, the conversation doesn't have to stop when the podcast is over.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢《心理学对话》，当播客结束时，对话不必停止。

sentences.zh: 只需支付一个低廉的价格注册参加美国心理学会2020年虚拟大会，即可无限次观看数百个关于心理学最新进展的视频。

sentences.en: Start with some of our selected videos featuring psychology's biggest names discussing such issues as COVID-19, racism and stigma.
sentences.zh: 从我们精选的一些视频开始，这些视频由心理学界的知名人物主讲，讨论诸如COVID-19、种族主义和污名化等问题。

sentences.en: Or let your curiosity take over and use our on-demand library to explore any topic.
sentences.zh: 或者让你的好奇心占据主导，利用我们的点播库探索任何主题。

sentences.en: Go to convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 请访问 convention.apa.org 斜杠 podcaSt。

sentences.en: That's convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.
sentences.zh: That's convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Nancy Siegel, a professor of psychology and director of the Twin Studies Center at California State University Fullerton.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是南希·西格尔博士，她是加州大学富勒顿分校的心理学教授兼双胞胎研究中心主任。

sentences.en: She has spent her entire career studying twins, beginning with her work on the Minnesota study of twins reared apart in the 1980s and 90s.
sentences.zh: 她的整个职业生涯都在研究双胞胎，始于20世纪80和90年代对明尼苏达州分开抚养的双胞胎研究的工作。

sentences.en: Today, she continues to study identical and fraternal twins, twins reared apart, and other unusual pairings, as she calls them, even unrelated people who look like twins.
sentences.zh: 今天，她继续研究同卵和异卵双胞胎、分开抚养的双胞胎，以及她所说的一些不同寻常的组合，甚至包括长得像双胞胎的毫无血缘关系的人。

sentences.en: She's written six books about twins and twin research and is working on a seventh.
sentences.zh: 她已经写了六本关于双胞胎和双胞胎研究的书，目前正在写第七本。

sentences.en: She is also, as it happens, a twin herself.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，她本人也是一名双胞胎。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Siegel.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学对话》，西格尔博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Let's start with a broad question.
sentences.zh: 让我们从一个广泛的问题开始。

sentences.en: Twin studies have a long history in psychology.
sentences.zh: 双胞胎研究在心理学中有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: Why is that, and what have we learned over the years?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样，这些年来我们学到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, twin studies are fascinating, and it's a very simple and very elegant design.
sentences.zh: 嗯，双胞胎研究非常迷人，这是一个非常简单且非常优雅的设计。

sentences.en: One simply compares the resemblance of identical twins who share all their genes to the resemblance of fraternal twins who share half the genes on average.
sentences.zh: 人们只需比较共享所有基因的同卵双胞胎的相似性，与平均共享一半基因的异卵双胞胎的相似性。

sentences.en: For most measured traits, we find that identical twins are more alike than fraternal twins, which is consistent with the genetic influence on that behavior.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数测量的特征，我们发现同卵双胞胎比异卵双胞胎更相似，这与该行为受基因影响是一致的。

sentences.en: And there are many variations on what I just described, which is the classic twin method.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚描述的是经典双胞胎方法，在此基础上有许多变体。

sentences.en: But as you said in your introduction, we study twins reared apart.
sentences.zh: 但正如你在介绍中所说，我们研究分开抚养的双胞胎。

sentences.en: We can study twins living apart for long periods of time.
sentences.zh: 我们可以研究长期分开生活的双胞胎。

sentences.en: And I have also been studying some very unusual pairings, which I hope we have time to get into.
sentences.zh: 我一直在研究一些非常不同寻常的组合，希望我们有时间展开谈谈。

sentences.en: I'm sure we will.
sentences.zh: 我相信会的。

sentences.en: So you've been studying twins since the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 所以你从20世纪80年代就开始研究双胞胎了。

sentences.en: How have the questions that you and other researchers asked changed over time as our understanding of genetics has become more sophisticated?
sentences.zh: 随着我们对遗传学的理解变得越来越复杂，你和其他研究人员提出的问题随着时间的推移发生了怎样的变化？

sentences.en: For example, a recent article in The Atlantic talked about how twin studies are advancing our understanding of epigenetics or how genes are expressed.
sentences.zh: 例如，《大西洋月刊》最近的一篇文章探讨了双胞胎研究如何推进我们对表观遗传学或基因如何表达的理解。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering if you can explain what that means.
sentences.zh: 所以我想知道你是否能解释一下这意味着什么。

sentences.en: Yes, sure.
sentences.zh: 好的，当然。

sentences.en: But let me just back up for a second.
sentences.zh: 但请允许我先退一步。

sentences.en: You wanted to talk about how questions and interests and focus has changed in twin studies over the years.
sentences.zh: 你刚才想讨论多年来双胞胎研究中的问题、兴趣和焦点是如何变化的。

sentences.en: So when I began in the 1980s, this was just when behavioral genetics was being admitted into the mainstream of psychology.
sentences.zh: 当我于20世纪80年代开始时，正值行为遗传学被心理学主流接纳之际。

sentences.en: And so investigators were interested in establishing a genetic basis for human behavior.
sentences.zh: 因此，研究人员有兴趣为人类行为确立遗传基础。

sentences.en: And twin studies and adoption studies were a very effective way to go.
sentences.zh: 双胞胎研究和领养研究是非常有效的方法。

sentences.en: Then things began to change and people began looking to see if they could find the actual genes that were linked to behaviors.
sentences.zh: 然后事情开始改变，人们开始寻找能否找到与行为相关的实际基因。

sentences.en: And that's partly where epigenetics comes in.
sentences.zh: 这也是表观遗传学发挥作用的部分原因。

sentences.en: Now, epigenetics refers to the turning on and turning off of genes.
sentences.zh: 现在，表观遗传学指的是基因的开启和关闭。

sentences.en: What environmental triggers, either before birth or sometime after birth, will activate a gene or perhaps silence it.
sentences.zh: 出生前或出生后的某些环境触发因素，会如何激活某个基因或将其沉默。

sentences.en: And this is where identical twins who differ in fundamental ways may be of greatest use to us in the medical sciences.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，在根本上有差异的同卵双胞胎可能对我们在医学科学中最有用。

sentences.en: Because we know that the similarity rate for identical twins are diabetes and multiple sclerosis is only 50%.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道，同卵双胞胎患糖尿病和多发性硬化症的相似率只有50%。

sentences.en: Schizophrenia may be 40%.
sentences.zh: 精神分裂症可能是40%。

sentences.en: So if they come into the world with the same genes, why is it that one twin expresses it and the other one does not?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果他们带着相同的基因来到这个世界，为什么一个双胞胎表现出来而另一个没有？

sentences.en: This is information that we can all use to assist individuals who are affected in the non-twin population.
sentences.zh: 这些信息都是我们可以用来帮助非双胞胎人群中受影响个人的。

sentences.en: And epigenetics came into play when Scott Kelly went into space, for example, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，当斯科特·凯利进入太空时，表观遗传学就派上用场了，对吧？

sentences.en: He's an identical twin and his brother was on Earth.
sentences.zh: 他是一个同卵双胞胎，他的兄弟在地球上。

sentences.en: And when Scott Kelly came back, he had gone through some genetic changes.
sentences.zh: 当斯科特·凯利回来时，他经历了一些基因变化。

sentences.en: Can you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Yes, he did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实经历了。

sentences.en: The flight travel that Scott Kelly took had him up at the International Space Station for almost a year while his twin brother, Mark, remained on Earth.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·凯利的飞行之旅使他在国际空间站呆了将近一年，而他的双胞胎兄弟马克则留在地球上。

sentences.en: And prior to the trip, they both had completed a very comprehensive set of tests, intellectual, physical, genetic, things of that sort.
sentences.zh: 在旅行之前，他们都完成了一套非常全面的测试，包括智力、身体、遗传以及诸如此类的测试。

sentences.en: And they found that contrary to expectation, it seemed that Scott Kelly's chromosomes actually reflected greater longevity.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，与预期相反，斯科特·凯利的染色体似乎实际上反映了更长的寿命。

sentences.en: One would expect that they should have not shown that.
sentences.zh: 人们本会预期他们不应该表现出这一点。

sentences.en: But most of his epigenetic changes have reverted back to what they were normally.
sentences.zh: 但他大部分的表观遗传变化已经恢复到正常状态。

sentences.en: But that is a fascinating study because we will never again get two identical twins who are both astronauts and one willing to take the trip.
sentences.zh: 但这却是一个极具吸引力的研究，因为我们再也不会有两个同卵双胞胎，既都是宇航员，又有一个愿意进行这次旅行。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: And is that common with epigenetics that things revert?
sentences.zh: 表观遗传学中的这种恢复正常现象常见吗？

sentences.en: It's trait specific.
sentences.zh: 这是因特征而异的。

sentences.en: It's trait specific.
sentences.zh: 这是因特征而异的。

sentences.en: One wouldn't really know that.
sentences.zh: 人们对此并不会真正了解。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Identical twins are not exact copies of each other in the sense that you've studied some identical twins who show a fair amount of physical variation,
sentences.zh: 同卵双胞胎并不是彼此的精确复制品，因为你研究过的一些同卵双胞胎表现出相当大的身体差异，

sentences.en: such as differences in height or hair color.
sentences.zh: 例如身高或发色上的差异。

sentences.en: What are the causes of these variations?
sentences.zh: 这些差异的原因是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the causes of variation are many.
sentences.zh: 嗯，造成差异的原因有很多。

sentences.en: If you talk about height and weight, it probably has to do with prenatal nutrition that might have been unequally distributed between the two twins.
sentences.zh: 如果你谈论身高和体重，它可能与产前营养有关，这些营养在两个双胞胎之间可能分配不均。

sentences.en: If identical twins share their blood systems, what we call fetal transfusion in the womb, that can also create differences in size and vigor, things like that sort.
sentences.zh: 如果同卵双胞胎共享血液系统，也就是我们在子宫内称之为胎儿输血的情况，这也可能造成体型和活力等方面的差异。

sentences.en: And if really to a severe degree, it might even lead to the demise of one of the twins.
sentences.zh: 如果严重到一定程度，甚至可能导致其中一个双胞胎夭折。

sentences.en: And then I mentioned the epigenetics before.
sentences.zh: 然后我之前提到了表观遗传学。

sentences.en: If twins somehow get exposed to different environmental events, whether global or micro environmental events, this can also trigger something in one twin and on the other.
sentences.zh: 如果双胞胎以某种方式接触到不同的环境事件，无论是全局的还是微观环境事件，这也可能在一个双胞胎身上触发某些东西而在另一个身上则没有。

sentences.en: Genetically speaking, too, identical twins may not be exactly alike.
sentences.zh: 从遗传学上讲，同卵双胞胎也可能并非完全相同。

sentences.en: Sometimes there are errors in copying when cells replicate.
sentences.zh: 有时细胞复制时会出现复制错误。

sentences.en: And so there could be spontaneous mutations in one twin that the other twin does not have.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个双胞胎身上可能会发生另一个双胞胎没有的自发突变。

sentences.en: So identical twins are less alike than people think they are.
sentences.zh: 所以同卵双胞胎并没有人们想象的那么相似。

sentences.en: They're more alike than any other pair of people, but they are less alike than people think they are.
sentences.zh: 他们比任何其他一对人都更相似，但他们并没有人们想象的那么相似。

sentences.en: And that's what makes them so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这正是他们如此迷人的原因。

sentences.en: Now, I've seen in some interviews you've corrected people who have used the term nature versus nurture.
sentences.zh: 现在，我看到在一些采访中，你纠正过那些使用“先天与后天”这一术语的人。

sentences.en: Why do you think that term is inaccurate?
sentences.zh: 为什么你认为这个术语不准确？

sentences.en: It's inaccurate because it does not appreciate the interplay between nature and nurture.
sentences.zh: 它不准确是因为它没有认识到先天与后天之间的相互作用。

sentences.en: So we prefer to say nature dash nurture or nature via nurture or something of that sort.
sentences.zh: 所以我们更倾向于说先天连着后天，或者通过后天的先天，诸如此类。

sentences.en: We try to disentangle these effects in populations.
sentences.zh: 我们试图在人群中厘清这些效应。

sentences.en: So when we say that intelligence has a 75% genetic effect or height is 95%, we're not talking about a single individual.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们说智力有75%的遗传效应或身高有95%时，我们讨论的不是某个单一的个体。

sentences.en: We're talking about the variation in a population.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的是人群中的变异。

sentences.en: In a single person, you cannot separate out the two because genes and environments are inextricably intertwined.
sentences.zh: 对于单个人来说，你无法将这两者分开，因为基因和环境是密不可分的。

sentences.en: Now, you're a fraternal twin yourself.
sentences.zh: 现在，你自己就是一个异卵双胞胎。

sentences.en: How has that experience as a twin influenced your research?
sentences.zh: 作为双胞胎的这种经历是如何影响你的研究的？

sentences.en: Well, being a fraternal twin, I was always fascinated with being a twin, although I never got the adulations that identical twins get when people meet them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，作为一个异卵双胞胎，我一直对成为双胞胎很着迷，尽管我从未得到过当人们遇到同卵双胞胎时那种赞誉。

sentences.en: But I knew from a very early age that there had to be something fundamentally different about us because we shared so many experiences in common,
sentences.zh: 但我从小就知道，我们在本质上一定有某种不同，因为我们分享了如此多的共同经历，

sentences.en: and yet we were so different in appearance and our interests and tastes and things of that sort.
sentences.zh: 然而我们在外表、兴趣、品味以及诸如此类的事情上又是如此不同。

sentences.en: So I would say that it certainly propelled me into the field.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，这无疑把我推进了这个领域。

sentences.en: How it's influenced me, not really, because I let the data drive that.
sentences.zh: 至于它对我的影响，其实并没有，因为我是让数据来主导研究。

sentences.en: And I've been surprised sometimes by certain things and certain things I've expected have come true.
sentences.zh: 有时我对某些事情感到惊讶，而我所期待的一些事情也成真了。

sentences.en: But you have to keep an open mind.
sentences.zh: 但你必须保持开放的心态。

sentences.en: But I will say that being a twin has been a great advantage because in soliciting subjects for my projects, the minute they discover that I'm a twin,
sentences.zh: 不过我要说的是，身为双胞胎是一个巨大的优势，因为在为我的项目招募受试者时，他们一发现我是双胞胎，

sentences.en: it creates this bond that you just understand what's going on, that we share something fundamentally important.
sentences.zh: 就会产生一种纽带，你会立刻明白发生了什么，我们共享着某些至关重要的东西。

sentences.en: And that's been a real advantage.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个优势。

sentences.en: There are a lot of myths and legends out there about twins, that they've got some kind of a telepathic connection, that they can share secret language.
sentences.zh: 关于双胞胎有许多神话和传说，比如他们有一种心灵感应的联系，他们能共享秘密语言。

sentences.en: And I know one of your books is called Twin Myths, Conceptions, False Beliefs, Fables and Facts About Twins.
sentences.zh: 我知道你的其中一本书叫《双胞胎迷思：关于双胞胎的概念、错误信念、寓言和事实》。

sentences.en: What are some of the common myths that you address?
sentences.zh: 你探讨了哪些常见的迷思？

sentences.en: And do any of these have grains of truth?
sentences.zh: 这些当中有任何一丝真相吗？

sentences.en: Well, the ones that I address mostly are, I mean, there's so many, there must be about 70 that I deal with in the book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我主要探讨的那些，我的意思是，有太多了，我在书中处理的大概有70个。

sentences.en: But some people think that fraternal twinning skips generations.
sentences.zh: 但有些人认为异卵双胞胎会隔代遗传。

sentences.en: Now, is there a kernel of truth?
sentences.zh: 那么，这其中有一点点真相吗？

sentences.en: It could do that in some families, but there's no actual rule for that.
sentences.zh: 它在某些家庭中可能会这样做，但并没有实际的规律。

sentences.en: We know that fraternal twinning runs in families, but the actual mode of transmission has not been identified.
sentences.zh: 我们知道异卵双胞胎在家族中具有遗传倾向，但实际的传播方式尚未被确定。

sentences.en: Some people feel that identical twins should always be separated in school when they enter.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得同卵双胞胎在入学时应该总是分在不同的班级。

sentences.en: And I'm really against that.
sentences.zh: 我非常反对这一点。

sentences.en: I think you have to take every pair on a case by case basis.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须具体情况具体对待每一对双胞胎。

sentences.en: We don't have firm policies regarding singleton children.
sentences.zh: 我们对独生子女并没有硬性规定。

sentences.en: And I think that this treats twins unfairly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对双胞胎是不公平的。

sentences.en: Other myths that identical twinning does not run in families.
sentences.zh: 另一个迷思是同卵双胞胎不具有家族遗传性。

sentences.en: Now, we thought that for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们很长一段时间都这么认为。

sentences.en: And yet some recent research from Sweden and from Singapore, looking at inbred populations, has found that there are these pockets of people around the world, in India, in Iran,
sentences.zh: 然而，来自瑞典和新加坡的一些最新研究，在对近亲繁殖的人群进行观察时，发现在世界各地存在着这样的人群聚居地，比如在印度、伊朗，

sentences.en: where there are multi-generations of just identical twins.
sentences.zh: 那里有连续好几代都只有同卵双胞胎。

sentences.en: And so we think that within some families, there's this tendency toward zygotic splitting or splitting of the single fertilized egg.
sentences.zh: 因此我们认为，在某些家庭中，存在着这种朝向合子分裂或单个受精卵分裂的倾向。

sentences.en: In my study, well, it wasn't for a study, but it was for my book, Indivisible by Two.
sentences.zh: 在我的研究中，嗯，其实不是为了研究，而是为了我的书《二而为一》。

sentences.en: I, it was kind of a, it's an interesting book.
sentences.zh: 我，这有点像是一本有趣的图书。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a Oliver Sacks' The Man Must Took His Wife for a Hat book, but for twins, where I bring in the human interest and the science.
sentences.zh: 它有点像奥利弗·萨克斯的《错把妻子当帽子》那样的书，但这是关于双胞胎的，我把人类的兴趣和科学融为一体。

sentences.en: And one of the couples that I studied were actually a set of identical male twins married to a set of identical female twins.
sentences.zh: 我研究的一对夫妇实际上是一对同卵男双胞胎娶了一对同卵女双胞胎。

sentences.en: They lived very close by.
sentences.zh: 他们住得很近。

sentences.en: And one of the couples had identical twins.
sentences.zh: 其中一对夫妇生了同卵双胞胎。

sentences.en: And so that's twins having twins.
sentences.zh: 所以那是生双胞胎的双胞胎。

sentences.en: And in my book, Twin Mythconceptions, I have a photograph of identical twin women, each of whom had a pair of identical twins.
sentences.zh: 在我的书《双胞胎迷思》中，我有一张同卵双胞胎女性的照片，她们每个人都生了一对同卵双胞胎。

sentences.en: So it seems that there is some factor in some families that gives you this genetic tendency toward that kind of twinning.
sentences.zh: 因此，似乎在某些家庭中存在某种因素，赋予了你这种产生双胞胎的遗传倾向。

sentences.en: And that creates some kind of a, a weird relationship, right?
sentences.zh: 这产生了一种奇怪的关系，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the twins are, they're genetically the same.
sentences.zh: 因为双胞胎，他们在基因上是一样的。

sentences.en: I mean, is it, so it's your uncle, you're also.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是，所以既是你的叔叔，你也是。

sentences.en: Well, well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Maybe you can explain this because I'm not doing a good job.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以解释一下，因为我没解释好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What happens is that if you have identical twins who marry identical twins, the offspring are legal first cousins,
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，如果你有同卵双胞胎娶了同卵双胞胎，他们的后代在法律上是表亲，

sentences.en: but they're also genetic full siblings because every parent is genetically interchangeable.
sentences.zh: 但他们在基因上也是亲兄弟姐妹，因为每一个父母在基因上都是可以互换的。

sentences.en: That's somewhat rare, but a much more common scenario is identical twins who just marry unrelated people.
sentences.zh: 这有点罕见，但更常见的情况是同卵双胞胎只是娶了或嫁给没有血缘关系的人。

sentences.en: And their children would be genetic half siblings in addition to being cousins.
sentences.zh: 除了作为表亲之外，他们的孩子在基因上将是半同胞关系。

sentences.en: But I will tell you one story that I have also in one of my books.
sentences.zh: 但我会告诉你一个我也写进我的书里的故事。

sentences.en: I think it was in Entwined Lives, my first one.
sentences.zh: 我想那是在我的第一本书《交织的人生》里。

sentences.en: I have a set of identical twins who married identical twins, and they had children on the same day, which makes them genetically equivalent to fraternal twins.
sentences.zh: 我有一对同卵双胞胎娶了同卵双胞胎，他们在同一天生了孩子，这使得他们在基因上等同于异卵双胞胎。

sentences.en: But see, they're enormously informative from the point of view of research because you've got people who are, who, you know,
sentences.zh: 但你看，从研究的角度来看，他们提供了非常丰富的信息，因为你拥有这样的人，他们，你知道的

sentences.en: you can look at the relation between say a twin aunt and a twin mother towards children.
sentences.zh: 你可以看看诸如双胞胎姑姑和双胞胎母亲与孩子之间的关系。

sentences.en: And they share the same genes, but, but one is raised with one and one is not raised with the other.
sentences.zh: 他们分享相同的基因，但是，其中一个和其中一个人一起长大，另一个则没有。

sentences.en: So you can look at all sorts of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以研究各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: Wow, that's wild.
sentences.zh: 哇，那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I can't imagine doing that genealogy.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象去做那样的家谱研究。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So you address the question about twins, whether they should be in the same classrooms during their education.
sentences.zh: 所以你探讨了关于双胞胎的问题，他们是否应该在教育期间分在同一个班级。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's something that you've looked at.
sentences.zh: 那是你研究过的一个课题。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, you know, when I grew up, there were, there were twins in my school and parents always dress their kids the same.
sentences.zh: 我在想，你知道的，我长大的时候，学校里有双胞胎，父母总是把他们的孩子打扮得一模一样。

sentences.en: Is there anything potentially damaging to children who don't get their identity, their, their own identity, because they're always dressed like their twin?
sentences.zh: 对于那些由于总是穿着和双胞胎一样的衣服而无法获得自己独立身份的孩子来说，这是否有什么潜在的伤害？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think that can be a problem.
sentences.zh: 对的，嗯，我认为这可能是一个问题。

sentences.en: And so I always encourage parents to dress the kids somewhat differently, maybe in the same outfits with contrasting colors, to have a name badge, cut the hair a bit differently,
sentences.zh: 所以我总是鼓励父母把孩子打扮得略有不同，比如穿颜色对比鲜明的同款服装，戴上名牌，头发剪得稍微有些区别，

sentences.en: so that people will call them by their name and not by twin or hey you.
sentences.zh: 这样人们就会叫他们的名字，而不是叫双胞胎或者“喂，你”。

sentences.en: I think, though, that twins should be allowed to enjoy their similarities at times if they want to dress up alike on occasion, nothing wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为，如果双胞胎偶尔想穿得一样，应该允许他们享受自己的相似之处，这没什么不对的。

sentences.en: But you don't want them to rely on that to get attention from other people.
sentences.zh: 但你不想让他们依靠这一点来获得其他人的关注。

sentences.en: The twin birth rate has more than doubled from 1980 to 2007, although it declined a little bit since then.
sentences.zh: 从1980年到2007年，双胞胎出生率增长了一倍多，尽管此后略有下降。

sentences.en: What's caused the shifts in the rate of twinning and have you seen any corresponding interest in your work as a result of that over the years?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了双胞胎出生率的变化？多年来，你的工作是否因此受到了相应的关注？

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So in 1980, the twinning rate was about one in 60 babies.
sentences.zh: 所以，在1980年，双胞胎出生率大约是六十分之一。

sentences.en: And later on, 20 years later, 30 years later, it was one in 33.
sentences.zh: 后来，20年、30年后，变成了三十三分之一。

sentences.en: And the reason it's gone up so much is because women are delaying their childbearing years, which creates a greater tendency for fraternal twinning.
sentences.zh: 它之所以上升这么多，是因为女性推迟了生育年龄，这导致怀上异卵双胞胎的倾向更大。

sentences.en: After all, for older mothers, you know, mistakes happen and we are optimally designed to release one egg at a time.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，对于年长的母亲来说，你知道的，意外会发生，我们被优化设计为一次只排一个卵子。

sentences.en: So two eggs at a time is kind of this mistake, although kind of a pleasant mistake, but it's still something that's not supposed to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以一次排两个卵子有点像这种失误，虽然算是一个令人愉快的失误，但它依然是不该发生的事情。

sentences.en: So that's one reason.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个原因。

sentences.en: Another is that we're better able to manage twin pregnancies now so we can detect them and manage them better.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是，我们现在更能掌控双胞胎妊娠了，因此我们可以更好地检测和管理它们。

sentences.en: And then with the in vitro fertilization, if women delay childbearing for too many years and they're unable to conceive, then they sometimes go the route of in vitro fertilization,
sentences.zh: 然后通过体外受精，如果女性推迟生育太多年而无法怀孕，那么她们有时会选择体外受精这条路，

sentences.en: where eggs and sperm are united outside the womb and then later implanted.
sentences.zh: 也就是卵子和精子在子宫外结合，然后再植入体内。

sentences.en: And that also has increased not just the fraternal and twinning rate, but also the identical twinning rate, although not as dramatically.
sentences.zh: 这也提高了异卵双胞胎的发病率，同时也提高了同卵双胞胎的发病率，尽管没有那么显著。

sentences.en: Now, the great rise in twinning, of course, has focused attention on twins so much.
sentences.zh: 现在，双胞胎的大幅增加，当然让人们对双胞胎投入了极大的关注。

sentences.en: We see them in literature, we see them in the news, TV commercials all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们一直能在文学作品、新闻、电视广告中看到他们。

sentences.en: People are fascinated with it.
sentences.zh: 人们对此着迷。

sentences.en: And I think that leads to another interesting idea.
sentences.zh: 我认为这引出了另一个有趣的想法。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why are people fascinated?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们会着迷？

sentences.en: So I began asking people and they'd say, well, they just are.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始问人们，他们会说，嗯，就是这样。

sentences.en: They're fascinating.
sentences.zh: 他们很迷人。

sentences.en: But I could not get an answer.
sentences.zh: 但我得不到答案。

sentences.en: So I've thought a lot about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我思考了很多。

sentences.en: And I think it's because we all are raised to appreciate individual differences in appearance and in behavior.
sentences.zh: 我想这是因为我们从小就被教育去欣赏外表和行为上的个体差异。

sentences.en: So when we encounter two people who look and act so much alike, it challenges our beliefs and how the world works.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们遇到两个长相和行为如此相似的人时，它挑战了我们的信念以及世界运转的方式。

sentences.en: And some people find it, well, everyone finds it intriguing.
sentences.zh: 有些人发现，呃，每个人都觉得这很吸引人。

sentences.en: Some people find it a little upsetting to see that much closeness.
sentences.zh: 有些人看到这么亲密的接触会感到有点不安。

sentences.en: But I think that's the clue.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这就是线索。

sentences.en: And with Twins Raised Apart, you know, we have such a strong reverence for family.
sentences.zh: 对于异地抚养的双胞胎，你知道的，我们对家庭有着如此强烈的崇敬。

sentences.en: The idea of these two very close people being raised apart just does not sit well.
sentences.zh: 这两个如此亲密的人被分开抚养的想法实在是让人无法接受。

sentences.en: And when we hear about the reunions, they're just so heartwarming.
sentences.zh: 当我们听到重聚的故事时，它们是如此温暖人心。

sentences.en: I have a whole series of tapes of twins meeting for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我有一整套双胞胎初次见面的录像带。

sentences.en: And I've seen it so many times.
sentences.zh: 我已经看过很多次了。

sentences.en: And every time I tear up, it's just that moment of me, that out of control glee is just amazing.
sentences.zh: 每次我都热泪盈眶，那种我终于找到你的时刻，那种无法控制的狂喜真是太棒了。

sentences.en: That's got to be a lot of fun when you go through life thinking that it's just you and then you discover…
sentences.zh: 当你一辈子都以为只有自己一个，然后突然发现……那一定很有趣。

sentences.en: It's you and me.
sentences.zh: 是你和我。

sentences.en: There's another one like me, yeah.
sentences.zh: 还有一个像我一样的人，是的。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So let's talk a little bit about the research projects you have going on now.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈你目前正在进行的科研项目吧。

sentences.en: You're continuing to study Twins Reared Apart, right?
sentences.zh: 你还在继续研究异地抚养的双胞胎，对吗？

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I have a study ongoing that looks at young Chinese twins who've been separated at birth indirectly through the one child policy.
sentences.zh: 我有一个正在进行的研究，关注的是因计划生育政策而间接在出生时被分开的中国年轻双胞胎。

sentences.en: And I get them.
sentences.zh: 我找到了他们。

sentences.en: It's the only prospective study in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上唯一的前瞻性研究。

sentences.en: Most Reared Apart twins studies have found twins as adults and had to reconstruct their childhood events.
sentences.zh: 大多数异地抚养双胞胎的研究都是在双胞胎成年后才找到他们，并不得不重构他们的童年经历。

sentences.en: But I'm getting the twins over time.
sentences.zh: 但我是在随着时间推移接触这些双胞胎。

sentences.en: Every pair has now had about two assessments, although I'm still completing the second one for some of the pairs.
sentences.zh: 现在每对双胞胎都已经接受了大约两次评估，尽管我仍在为其中一些对双胞胎完成第二次评估。

sentences.en: And so the twins live with different families in the U.S., sometimes in Canada or other places around the world.
sentences.zh: 所以这些双胞胎和美国的不同家庭住在一起，有时在加拿大或世界其他地方。

sentences.en: And so I'm able to get the twins tested in their local areas.
sentences.zh: 因此我能够在他们当地对双胞胎进行测试。

sentences.en: And parents fill out questionnaires.
sentences.zh: 父母会填写问卷。

sentences.en: Now the kids are growing up, so I can do a little more with them.
sentences.zh: 现在孩子们长大了，所以我可以对他们做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And I've studied 23 pairs of them so far, 15 identicals and eight fraternals.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我已经研究了23对双胞胎，其中15对同卵，8对异卵。

sentences.en: And I just hope I can continue because grant money is scarce.
sentences.zh: 我只希望我能继续下去，因为资助资金很紧缺。

sentences.en: But I would just love to find some more.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想找到更多。

sentences.en: I really would.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。

sentences.en: Now, I also do case studies on adult twins who find each other.
sentences.zh: 现在，我也对互相找到彼此的成年双胞胎进行个案研究。

sentences.en: And I've got one right now.
sentences.zh: 我手头正好有一个。

sentences.en: These twins from South Korea just met each other just in the last week or so.
sentences.zh: 来自韩国的这对双胞胎就在过去一周左右刚刚见面。

sentences.en: And I'm so excited.
sentences.zh: 我太兴奋了。

sentences.en: And so I have a colleague in South Korea who will test the South Korean twin.
sentences.zh: 所以在韩国有一位同事会去测试那个韩国双胞胎。

sentences.en: And I'm going to test the twin who lives here.
sentences.zh: 而我将测试住在这里的双胞胎。

sentences.en: And they didn't know about the other?
sentences.zh: 他们不知道对方的存在吗？

sentences.en: No, they didn't know about the other until...
sentences.zh: 不，他们不知道对方的存在，直到……

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: Well, the one in South Korea knew.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在韩国的那个人是知道的。

sentences.en: Because what happened there was that she was out with...
sentences.zh: 因为当时的情况是她和……

sentences.en: Well, the mother had twins.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这位母亲生了双胞胎。

sentences.en: She obviously knew that.
sentences.zh: 她显然是知道的。

sentences.en: The twins are maybe two or three.
sentences.zh: 双胞胎当时可能两三岁。

sentences.en: And the grandmother took one twin out on a walk or something and lost her in a market and never found her again.
sentences.zh: 祖母带着其中一个双胞胎去散步什么的，在市场上弄丢了，再也没有找到。

sentences.en: And the twin ended up back in an orphanage and was adopted.
sentences.zh: 这个双胞胎最终回到了孤儿院并被收养了。

sentences.en: But she never knew she was a twin until she did...
sentences.zh: 但她从不知道自己有个双胞胎姐妹，直到她做了……

sentences.en: It's a program now for Korean adopters.
sentences.zh: 现在有一个针对韩国被收养者的项目。

sentences.en: They can submit their DNA and see if it matches.
sentences.zh: 他们可以提交自己的DNA看看是否能配对。

sentences.en: And that's how she found her family.
sentences.zh: 这就是她找到家人方式。

sentences.en: I'm also fascinated by a study you did a few years ago on doppelgangers.
sentences.zh: 我对你几年前做的一项关于大众脸（双胞胎般的陌生人）的研究也很着迷。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: People who are completely unrelated, but they look uncannily alike.
sentences.zh: 那些完全没有亲缘关系，但长相却出奇相似的人。

sentences.en: Why were you interested in studying this phenomenon and what did you learn?
sentences.zh: 你为什么对研究这个现象感兴趣？你学到了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: See, there was a criticism of twin research held by some that identical twins are alike in personality because people treat them a certain way based on their looks.
sentences.zh: 你看，有些人对双胞胎研究提出过批评，认为同卵双胞胎性格相似是因为人们根据他们的外表以某种方式对待他们。

sentences.en: And that never made sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说从来都讲不通。

sentences.en: It just never made sense to me.
sentences.zh: 它根本就说不通。

sentences.en: I think what happens is that people respond similarly to identical twins, but because they evoke certain reactions from these people.
sentences.zh: 我认为实际情况是，人们对同卵双胞胎的反应相似，是因为他们从这些人身上唤起了某些反应。

sentences.en: So the way to test that, I realized, was to use unrelated people who shared no genes but shared their looks.
sentences.zh: 所以我意识到，检验这一点的方法是使用没有基因联系但长相相似的无关人员。

sentences.en: And so I reasoned that if they were as alike as identical twins raised apart, well, then maybe I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 因此我推断，如果他们像异地抚养的同卵双胞胎一样相似，好吧，那可能是我错了。

sentences.en: But if they were very different, then it would mean that their genetics were so different that they were not going to be similar in personality.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们截然不同，那就意味着他们的基因差异太大，以至于他们的性格不会相似。

sentences.en: And so I worked with somebody in Canada, a photographer, Francois Brunel, who takes photographs of these people.
sentences.zh: 所以我与加拿大的一位摄影师弗朗索瓦·布内尔（Francois Brunel）合作，他拍摄这些人的照片。

sentences.en: He's a photographer.
sentences.zh: 他是一名摄影师。

sentences.en: I think he was a doppelganger himself.
sentences.zh: 我想他自己就是一个大众脸。

sentences.en: And so I got some of my people from him.
sentences.zh: 所以我的一些研究对象是从他那里找来的。

sentences.en: And then a British television show gave me eight pairs.
sentences.zh: 然后一个英国电视节目给了我八对。

sentences.en: And I find them occasionally.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔也会找到他们。

sentences.en: Here and there I find them.
sentences.zh: 这里一个，那里一个。

sentences.en: And they're just amazing.
sentences.zh: 他们真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: And so I published two or three papers on these cases.
sentences.zh: 所以我针对这些案例发表了两三篇论文。

sentences.en: And I find that these doppelgangers who were raised apart but look exactly alike are so different than personality.
sentences.zh: 我发现这些异地抚养、长相一模一样的大众脸，性格却大不相同。

sentences.en: And when they meet, they don't feel a certain kinship.
sentences.zh: 当他们见面时，他们不会感到某种亲缘关系。

sentences.en: The identical twins feel it almost instantly.
sentences.zh: 同卵双胞胎几乎瞬间就能感受到。

sentences.en: These people are sort of curious and maybe it lasts for a minute, but it doesn't laSt.
sentences.zh: 这些人有点好奇，也许这种感觉能持续一分钟，但不会持久。

sentences.en: And do they actually see the resemblance?
sentences.zh: 他们真的能看到相似之处吗？

sentences.en: Do they always get it?
sentences.zh: 他们总是能认出来吗？

sentences.en: Sometimes and sometimes not.
sentences.zh: 有时能，有时不能。

sentences.en: You know, this is another interesting thing that sometimes if you talk to identical twins, they don't think they look alike.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这又是另一个有趣的事情，有时如果你和同卵双胞胎谈话，他们并不觉得自己长得像。

sentences.en: It's a very, very funny thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: So how do you find participants in your studies?
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何在研究中寻找参与者的呢？

sentences.en: Is the Internet making it easier?
sentences.zh: 互联网让这变得更容易了吗？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely it is.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I really have never solicited people.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我真的从未主动招募过人。

sentences.en: People come to me.
sentences.zh: 都是人们主动来找我。

sentences.en: I feel like Sir Francis Galton back in the 1870s when people would say, I want to be in your studies.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己就像19世纪70年代的弗朗西斯·高尔顿爵士，当时人们会说，我想参加你的研究。

sentences.en: And I mean, I'm just getting people all the time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我无时无刻不在接收到这样的人。

sentences.en: It's just amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: I'm lucky that I have an international network.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运拥有一个国际网络。

sentences.en: People send me emails and contacts all the time.
sentences.zh: 人们随时会给我发电子邮件和联系方式。

sentences.en: I found one of my most interesting pairs.
sentences.zh: 我找到了我最有趣的一对双胞胎。

sentences.en: Well, actually, the situation in Columbia, South America, involving two sets of identical male twins who'd been accidentally switched at birth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，在南美洲的哥伦比亚，有两对在出生时被意外调包的同卵男双胞胎。

sentences.en: So there was an exchange of one twin from each pair.
sentences.zh: 所以每对双胞胎中都有一个被调换了。

sentences.en: And they grew up in very different environments.
sentences.zh: 他们在非常不同的环境中长大。

sentences.en: And when I learned about this through a colleague, I went right down to Bogota to study them.
sentences.zh: 当我通过一位同事得知这件事后，我立刻前往波哥大去研究他们。

sentences.en: And it was a book came out of that called Accidental Brothers published in 2018.
sentences.zh: 由此诞生了一本书，名为《意外的兄弟》，于2018年出版。

sentences.en: But let me get back a minute to that, to the studies of the studies of twins raised apart.
sentences.zh: 但让我花一分钟回到那个话题，关于异地抚养双胞胎的研究。

sentences.en: I think it's also important to recognize that twin studies have had a wonderful history, but there have been a couple of blemishes along the way.
sentences.zh: 我认为同样重要的是认识到双胞胎研究有着辉煌的历史，但在过程中也存在一些瑕疵。

sentences.en: And the book that you mentioned earlier that I'm writing right now, my seventh, it's actually all written in the hands of the editor.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到我正在写的书，也就是我的第七本，其实已经全部写完并在编辑手里了。

sentences.en: So I'm, I'm a free person, but that one is going to be called deliberately divided inside the controversial study of twins and triplets adopted apart.
sentences.zh: 所以我是个自由人了，但那本书将被称为《故意拆散：被收养的双胞胎与三胞胎的争议研究内幕》。

sentences.en: They'll be out in the spring of 2021.
sentences.zh: 它将于2021年春季出版。

sentences.en: And I think that most of your viewers have probably seen or at least heard about the documentary film Three Identical Strangers that talked about identical triplets who were separated and in a secret study.
sentences.zh: 我想你们大多数观众可能看过或者至少听说过纪录片《三个相同的陌生人》，它讲述了被分开并参与秘密研究的同卵三胞胎。

sentences.en: So I went back and I researched that study, the history, the origins, the implications, all the people, and the legal and ethical implications.
sentences.zh: 所以我回头研究了那项研究、它的历史、起源、影响、所有相关人员，以及法律和伦理影响。

sentences.en: And so it's a pretty big book, but it had to be written.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一本相当大的书，但它必须被写出来。

sentences.en: It had to preserve all of that.
sentences.zh: 它必须保存所有这些历史。

sentences.en: And it was a tribute to the twins who were separated at birth, who never, who were separated because a researcher or a psychiatrist felt it was better for them.
sentences.zh: 这是对在出生时被分离的双胞胎的致敬，他们之所以被分离，是因为研究人员或精神病学家认为这对他们更好。

sentences.en: I mean, it just, there was no literature to support that whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根本没有任何文献来支持这一点。

sentences.en: And yeah, tell us a little bit more about this, this psychiatriSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，跟我们多讲讲这位精神病学家吧。

sentences.en: His name was Peter Neubauer, right?
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫彼得·纽鲍尔（Peter Neubauer），对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: Well, there were two psychiatrists.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时有两位精神病学家。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Dr. Viola Bernard was the, she was the psychiatrist that had been, that had been hired by the Louise Wise Agency.
sentences.zh: 维奥拉·伯纳德医生，她就是曾受雇于路易丝·怀斯机构的那位精神病学家。

sentences.en: And just to, you know, to give advice on adoptions and things.
sentences.zh: 她当时只是，你知道的，就收养等问题提供一些咨询意见。

sentences.en: And she felt that identical twins or even any twins should be raised apart so they develop their own identities and parents would not be overburdened.
sentences.zh: 她认为同卵双胞胎甚至任何双胞胎都应该分开抚养，这样他们才能培养各自的个性，父母也不会不堪重负。

sentences.en: But there was, there was no literature to support that.
sentences.zh: 但当时并没有相关的文献来支持这一点。

sentences.en: Absolutely none.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有。

sentences.en: But that went on nevertheless.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，这种做法还是进行了下去。

sentences.en: And then this other psychiatrist, Peter Neubauer, discovered this and he decided to study the twins.
sentences.zh: 然后另一位精神病学家彼得·纽鲍尔发现了这一点，他决定对这些双胞胎进行研究。

sentences.en: It was a collaboration.
sentences.zh: 这是一次合作。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to know which came first, the study, the theory.
sentences.zh: 而且真的很难搞清楚哪个是先出来的，是研究还是理论。

sentences.en: I mean, it's difficult to know exactly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很难确切知道。

sentences.en: And I talk all about that in the book.
sentences.zh: 我在书中详细讨论了这一切。

sentences.en: And so the twins were studied from the time of birth until 12 years.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些双胞胎从出生起一直被研究到12岁。

sentences.en: And of course, the data are locked up at Yale and not to be sealed until 2065.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些数据都被封存在耶鲁大学，直到2065年才会解密。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's another issue I deal with.
sentences.zh: 这是我处理的另一个问题。

sentences.en: And some of Dr. Bernard's materials at Columbia have been sealed too, but there's enough available there that I was able to really get a lot of material.
sentences.zh: 伯纳德医生在哥伦比亚大学的一些材料也被封存了，但那里有足够多的可用资料，让我能够获取大量素材。

sentences.en: I look forward to seeing that.
sentences.zh: 我很期待看到那些。

sentences.en: So what are the remaining unanswered questions in the field?
sentences.zh: 那么，该领域目前还剩下哪些未解之谜？

sentences.en: What do we still don't know?
sentences.zh: 还有什么是我们依然不知道的？

sentences.en: I'm sure there are many, many, but maybe you can give us a few.
sentences.zh: 我确信有很多很多，但也许你可以给我们讲几个。

sentences.en: Well, you know, one very vexing question that's still never been answered satisfactorily is why does the fertilized egg divide?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，有一个非常令人困惑且至今未得到满意解答的问题，就是受精卵为什么会分裂？

sentences.en: What causes the divide?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了分裂？

sentences.en: There are theories about it, but we really do not know.
sentences.zh: 虽然有关于这方面的理论，但我们确实不知道。

sentences.en: We really do not know.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道。

sentences.en: And it used to be thought that the timing of the split from conception until day 14 had to do with the number of placenta and the number of field membranes.
sentences.zh: 过去人们认为，从受孕到第14天分裂的时间点，与胎盘数量以及胚膜数量有关。

sentences.en: But even that is in dispute.
sentences.zh: 但连这一点也存在争议。

sentences.en: So it's really, really quite fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很奇妙、非常吸引人。

sentences.en: And anything else that's on the horizon that you want to tell our listeners about?
sentences.zh: 还有什么即将到来的趋势想和我们的听众分享吗？

sentences.en: Any other work that's percolating?
sentences.zh: 还有什么正在酝酿中的工作吗？

sentences.en: I think we're still going to continue with looking at how epigenetics is going to shape our understanding of human behavior and disease.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们仍将继续研究表观遗传学将如何塑造我们对人类行为和疾病的理解。

sentences.en: That's certainly going to take off.
sentences.zh: 这肯定会蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: But I think that it's also important to stay very close to twins just to get a sense of what they're like.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，与双胞胎保持紧密联系也很重要，这样才能了解他们的真实状态。

sentences.en: Because just being with them gives you so many great hypotheses about how things could happen.
sentences.zh: 因为仅仅和他们在一起，就能让你对事情如何发生产生许多极好的假设。

sentences.en: In Minnesota, for example, we used to see that identical twins had a lot of quirks in common.
sentences.zh: 例如，在明尼苏达州，我们过去常常发现同卵双胞胎有很多共同的怪癖。

sentences.en: We had a pair who used to read books from back to front, and he used to wash his hands before and after using the bathroom.
sentences.zh: 我们曾有一对双胞胎，其中一个习惯倒着看书，而且他上厕所前和上厕所后都要洗手。

sentences.en: All these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的各种事情。

sentences.en: And so when you see it in one person, you figure, well, it's just a habit.
sentences.zh: 所以当你只在一个人身上看到这种情况时，你会觉得，嗯，这只是一种习惯。

sentences.en: But with two people who do it, who were reared apart, you figure there has to be something more.
sentences.zh: 但当两个分开抚养的人都有这种做法时，你就会觉得其中一定有什么更深层的原因。

sentences.en: And so I think one of the projects I may attempt in the fall, I'm sorry, in the spring when I teach my graduate seminar on twin studies,
sentences.zh: 所以我想我在秋季——抱歉，是在春季当我教授双胞胎研究的研究生研讨班时，可能会尝试的一个项目是，

sentences.en: is I'm going to have my students go back to the older literature and document all of these unusual behaviors in the identical twins and some other ones.
sentences.zh: 我要让我的学生回过头去查阅旧文献，记录下同卵双胞胎以及其他双胞胎的所有这些不寻常的行为。

sentences.en: And we'll just see, you know, what are they?
sentences.zh: 然后我们拭目以待，看看它们到底是什么？

sentences.en: Can they be studied systematically?
sentences.zh: 它们能被系统地研究吗？

sentences.en: How do we explain them?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何解释它们？

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Siegel, this has been really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 西格尔博士，这次谈话真的太精彩了。

sentences.en: I think the research that you do is quite, quite amazing.
sentences.zh: 我认为你所做的研究非常非常了不起。

sentences.en: And I really appreciate your taking the time to talk to me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天抽出时间跟我聊聊。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或您获取播客的任何地方找到往期的《心理学热线》节目。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，请发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 地址是 speakingofpsychology，所有字母连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学热线》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Condayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频剪辑师是克里斯·孔戴安。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学会的金·米尔斯。
